_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma who received a prior anthracycline-containing regimen

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled trial of trabectedin 1.5 mg/m2 as a 24-hour continuous IV infusion every 3 weeks versus dacarbazine 1000 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with unresectable or metastatic leiomyosarcoma or liposarcoma with progression following prior anthracycline- and ifosfamide-containing regimen or an anthracycline-containing regimen plus one additional cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary study objective was overall survival (OS); the primary efficacy endpoint was changed to investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) after trial initiation
pivotal_trials.n: 518 patients randomized, 345 to trabectedin and 173 to dacarbazine
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant improvement in investigator-assessed PFS: median 4.2 vs 1.5 months, HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.44, 0.70); p<0.001. No OS benefit: median 13.7 vs 13.1 months, HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.75, 1.15); p=0.49

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): nausea, fatigue, vomiting, constipation, decreased appetite, diarrhea, peripheral edema, dyspnea, headache. Serious risks include neutropenic sepsis (Grade 3-4 neutropenia 43%, 161/378), rhabdomyolysis, hepatotoxicity, and cardiomyopathy
target_moa: Trabectedin is an alkylating drug that binds guanine residues in the minor groove of DNA, forming adducts and bending the DNA helix, triggering events affecting DNA binding proteins and DNA repair pathways, resulting in cell cycle perturbation and cell death

rems.type: REMS are not required to ensure safe use of trabectedin despite the serious risks of anaphylaxis, neutropenic sepsis, rhabdomyolysis, hepatotoxicity, cardiomyopathy and extravasation

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) because the safety profile was acceptable and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues

description.text: Updated Use in Specific Populations, adding Pregnancy Testing and pediatric study results to the Pediatric Use subsections

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the Use in Specific Populations section, including the addition of “Pregnancy Testing” under Females and Males of Reproductive Potential subsection and updates to the Pediatric Use subsections of the package insert (PI) to include the results from pediatric studies as part of the December 4, 2000, original Written Request for pediatric studies for Yondelis (trabectedin), our subsequent July 2, 2002, May 19, 2004, October 4, 2010, March 15, 2012, July 31, 2017, amended Written Request letters and, our November 7, 2017, reissued Written Request letter.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted September 30, 2004 for trabectedin for the treatment of soft tissue sarcoma

citations.quote: On September 30, 2004, FDA granted orphan drug designation for trabectedin for the treatment of soft tissue sarcoma.

summary.text: Regular approval of trabectedin based primarily on a single randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial (ET743-SAR-3007) demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in investigator-assessed PFS; the product had orphan drug designation for soft tissue sarcoma, and two postmarketing requirements (cardiomyopathy risk characterization and hepatic impairment PK) were imposed

citations.quote: This NDA is supported primarily by a single trial, Study ET743-SAR-3007, a randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled trial conducted in patients with unresectable or metastatic leiomyosarcoma or liposarcoma
On September 30, 2004, FDA granted orphan drug designation for trabectedin for the treatment of soft tissue sarcoma.
Two post-marketing requirement (PMR) trials have been identified by FDA under the provisions of the FDCA 505(o).

requirement.text: PMR 2964-1: Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data to characterize the risk of cardiomyopathy and its sequelae in patients receiving trabectedin, identify risk factors, and support labeling for dose modification and monitoring

citations.quote: 2964-1 Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from an adequate number of clinical trial(s) to characterize the risk of cardiomyopathy and its sequelae in patients receiving trabectedin; to identify risk factors for development of these sequelae; and to support labeling instructions for dose modification and monitoring.

requirement.text: PMR 2964-2: Submit the final report of the completed clinical pharmacokinetic trial to determine the pharmacokinetics of Yondelis (trabectedin) in patients with hepatic impairment

citations.quote: 2964-2 Submit the final report of the completed clinical pharmacokinetic trial to determine the pharmacokinetics of Yondelis (trabectedin) in patients with hepatic impairment in accordance with the FDA Guidance for Industry entitled **“Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic Function: Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing and Labeling.”**
